metadata.title: Household Finance Brokerage Platform Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how a Belgian omnichannel household-finance broker of about 200 people (head office Zaventem, customer care in Hasselt and Oujda), with more than 150 mortgage experts in about 70 largely franchised hypotheek.winkel offices, three comparison brands in Dutch and French, more than 50,000 contracts concluded per year with more than 50 bank, insurer, energy and telecom partners who pay a referral commission, backed by Vortex Capital Partners since 2020 and acquired by Meilleurtaux in December 2025, would need to change when a sharp mortgage rate rise contracts the market by roughly 40 percent again, a major bank cuts or re-tiers its broker commission, an IDD or Mortgage Credit Directive review bans commissions or mandates fee disclosure, an energy price shock or regulated tariff removes the switching gain, a Google core update and the public V-check drain traffic from the comparison brands, consumer AI agents compare offers directly, scarce FSMA-qualified experts and franchisee churn empty offices, a breach exposes credit files, the Meilleurtaux integration merges two networks and two workbenches, or a partner tariff or rate feed silently sells prices that do not exist.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A household runs a simulator on peasy.be, hypotheekwinkel.be, verzekeringen.be or aanbieders.be, books an appointment in the nearest office or a video call, or asks for a callback. The expert maps the buyer's project, compares the daily conditions of 25 banks on one screen, issues a feasibility certificate, collects the documents, submits the credit file to the chosen bank, follows approval, compromis and notary deed, and attaches outstanding-balance and fire insurance. Customer-care advisors in Hasselt and Oujda compare car, fire, funeral and outstanding-balance insurance across 11 insurers, electricity, gas, internet, TV and mobile, bind the policy or execute the switch and cancel the old contract. The brokered contracts land in a household vault that fires a savings alert when a better deal exists. Leads are routed to offices by postcode, franchisees see production and conversion dashboards, the academy trains about 30 advisors a year, partner catalogues and tariff feeds are ingested daily, and commissions from more than 50 partners are reconciled and paid out to the network. The design assumes that the mortgage market grows or at least holds, that a commission is a number per bank that arrives, that the consumer never pays and never needs to know what the partner pays, that a comparison is a ranking whose recommendation is always to switch, that demand comes from Google to three separate websites, that the comparison page is read by a human, that an office is a location with an expert who stays, that a credit file is a folder the office owns, that there is one company with one brand and one workbench in Dutch, and that a tariff feed is right when it arrives.
metadata.residualArchitecture: The changed design separates case type and demand mix per office, rate scenario and borrowing-capacity rule, office economics and commission forecast by pipeline stage and deed lag, partner agreement version with commission schedule, tiers, clawback rule and effective period, expected commission per file and statement reconciliation, payout rule per agreement version, bank concentration measure, remuneration source and disclosed amount per contract, consumer fee product and price schedule, advice record with remuneration disclosure and independence evidence, tariff version and validity window, market condition snapshot, comparison rule version, outcome type including stay, savings range and re-check date per household, revenue line per contract type, demand source and channel with cost per appointment, brand and domain routing with canonical content, owned-channel reach per household, comparison capability as a callable service with terms, agent channel and attribution, negotiated condition versus public tariff, AI-prepared draft with provenance and expert sign-off, expert capacity, skill and FSMA registration status, regional expert pool and video fallback, academy cohort and time-to-productive, office succession record, file continuity across experts, data class, access scope by file, task and period, step-up authentication event, view and export event, retention rule per data class, incident and affected-record set, franchise security obligation, brand, legal entity and network membership, shared customer and identity registry, concept mapping and migration lineage, agreement per legal entity with group view, locale as first-class, capability parity and sunset plan, and feed validation and quarantine. A proposal, a quote, a switch and an alert know which feed version, rule version, agreement and person produced them; an office is a coverage the network guarantees; a household can change brand, office, expert, partner or company without changing systems; and who pays for advice is a rule, not a fact about the trade.
metadata.note: The stressors start in the Belgian household-finance trade: the Febelfin figures for mortgage credit applications in 2023 (down roughly 37 percent in Q1 and 29 percent in Q2 against 2022) and the recovery from 2024, the referral commission model in which the bank's head office pays the broker and the consumer pays nothing extra, the FSMA registers of credit and insurance intermediaries and the IDD and Mortgage Credit Directive with the Dutch commission ban as the reference point, the 2022 energy price crisis, the VREG V-test and V-check with the invoice code mandatory since 1 July 2025 and Wikifin, consumer AI assistants, the scarce-skill status of the mortgage expert and the academy that trains about 30 advisors a year, GDPR and FSMA record-keeping, and the Meilleurtaux acquisition of December 2025 creating a group of 81 offices. They are not forecasts and assign no likelihood; each asks what must remain after the broker is pushed into a different attractor. The rate rise, commission cut, energy shock, advisor scarcity and breach scenarios are recorded as residues the platform already carries; the feed failure is the loop that tests whether the tariff-version and expected-commission residues hold without new structure.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: A sharp mortgage rate rise contracts the Belgian mortgage market by roughly 40 percent again
stressors.detection: The ECB rate path and Belgian long-term fixed mortgage rates rising within two quarters; Febelfin quarterly credit statistics of the kind that showed applications excluding refinancing down roughly 37 percent in Q1 2023 and 29 percent in Q2 2023 against 2022; simulator sessions rising while feasibility certificates fall; sellers refusing offers with a financing condition; banks tightening loan-to-value and debt-ratio criteria and declining files that passed a year earlier; appointments per office per month falling below the franchise business case; upload-your-proposal requests shifting from purchase to refinancing; expert utilisation dropping; franchisees asking head office for fee relief; and referral commissions, paid only at deed, falling a quarter after the appointments did.
stressors.attractor: Within two quarters the 20-year fixed rate doubles, the borrowing capacity of a couple falls by a fifth, sellers stop accepting offers with a financing condition, purchase files drop by 40 percent across about 70 offices, and each office runs on half the appointments the franchise business case assumed. Referral commissions fall with a lag, experts trained in the academy sit idle, and franchisees whose margin is the commission share hand back their offices. In the naive design an office is a fixed-cost location with a purchase target, the lead engine serves purchase appointments by postcode, the expert's file process assumes the bank will say yes, refinancing and renovation loans are side cases, the certificate does not say under which rate it was issued, and the commission forecast is a straight line from last year's deeds.
stressors.businessReaction: Keep investing through the downturn, as the group did, and give the network something to sell: route demand by case type so refinancing, renovation loans under the Flemish EPC obligation, second projects, self-employed financing and insurance and energy cross-sell fill the expert calendar; model office economics per office with commission share, lead cost and capacity so head office can support offices in trouble rather than lose them; compute borrowing capacity and feasibility per rate scenario in the simulators and on the certificate so buyers still get a document a seller trusts; forecast commissions by pipeline stage and expected deed date rather than by last year's volume; use the empty capacity to train and certify advisors for the recovery; and hold on to the household through contract monitoring when the mortgage does not close.
stressors.residue: Separate case type and demand mix per office, rate scenario and borrowing-capacity rule, certificate validity and rate stamp, office economics record, commission forecast by pipeline stage and deed lag, expert capacity and utilisation, and cross-sell path per household. An office is a capacity that serves whatever the market brings, not a purchase-loan target.

impacts.effect: First-time buyers still learn what they can borrow under the rate in force and get a certificate a seller trusts when the market stalls.
Franchisees see their office economics per case type and get support instead of a purchase target they cannot reach.
Refinancers and second-project owners become the demand the network is built to serve when purchases stall.
Borrowing capacity is computed per rate scenario so the buyer sees what a further rise does to the budget before bidding.
Refinancing and proposal reviews become a first-class demand source that fills experts when purchases fall.
An expert's calendar is fed with renovation, refinancing, self-employed and insurance cases when purchase appointments are scarce.
Production reporting shows the demand mix, utilisation and the commission lag, not only deed counts.
Days from first appointment to loan approval is read per rate scenario so a tighter bank does not look like a slower expert.
Office commission income is forecast from pipeline stages and expected deed dates rather than from last year's volume.
Serves refinancing, renovation and second-project cases with the same 25-bank comparison as a purchase.
States the rate scenario and validity date so a certificate issued before a rise is not read as a promise.
Adds office economics, downturn support and recovery training to the franchise dashboards.
Runs the simulation under the current and a stressed rate and stamps the certificate accordingly.
Becomes the demand channel that fills the network in a downturn.
Routes leads by case type and office capacity and reports office economics.
Computes borrowing capacity and monthly repayment per rate scenario.
Stamps the rate scenario and a validity date on every certificate.

stressors.name: A major bank cuts its broker commission or moves to a volume-tiered schedule with clawback
stressors.detection: A bank's head office announcing a new intermediary remuneration schedule; commission statements arriving with a lower rate or an unfamiliar tier; clawback lines for loans repaid or refinanced within the first years; a bank offering its direct customers a rate the broker channel does not get; the share of the network's files submitted to one bank; commission per file falling while file volume holds; franchisees noticing their payout drop before head office explains it; partner managers renegotiating one bank at a time from a PDF; and other banks watching what the first one gets away with.
stressors.attractor: One of the largest of the 25 banks announces that broker commissions fall by a third, that a tiered schedule rewards volumes the network cannot commit to, and that commissions on loans refinanced within three years are clawed back. The bank carries a fifth of the network's files; the offices that steer to it lose income overnight; and the independence the brand promises, the best total package at no extra cost, is questioned if experts stop recommending the bank or if they never stopped recommending it because it paid well. In the naive design the commission rate is a number per bank in a spreadsheet, the recommendation engine does not know what a bank pays and cannot prove it did not care, the payout to offices is a percentage of whatever arrives, and the partner contract is a PDF in a mailbox.
stressors.businessReaction: Model the partner agreement with its commission schedule, tiers, clawback rules and effective periods; compute the expected commission per file at submission and reconcile it against the statement line by line; keep the advice record explicit that the recommendation was made on the customer's total package, with the commission visible to compliance, so that independence is provable to the FSMA and to the customer; pay the network from a payout rule per agreement version rather than a flat share; spread volume across the 25 banks with a concentration watch per office; and negotiate with facts on volume, file completeness and approval rates the bank gets from the channel.
stressors.residue: Separate partner agreement version, commission schedule with tiers, clawback rule and effective period, expected commission per file, statement reconciliation, payout rule per agreement version, bank concentration measure, and independence evidence on the advice record. A commission is a computed expectation under an agreement, not a number that arrives.

impacts.effect: Lender partners negotiate on the file quality and approval rates the channel delivers, with every agreement version reconciled to the cent.
Franchisees see what each file should earn under the agreement in force and why a payout changed.
Broker-channel volume is planned against a tiered schedule the bank and the network both can see.
Reconciliation compares each statement line with the expected commission per file and raises disputes by agreement version.
Office commission reporting shows the agreement, tier and clawback behind every euro.
Independent advice is provable because the advice record separates the customer's package from what the bank pays.
Broker-channel value is measured per agreement version so a schedule change does not hide in the total.
Commission income and payout are tracked per agreement version, tier and clawback rule.

Keeps recommending the best total package with the remuneration recorded separately.

stressors.name: An IDD or Mortgage Credit Directive review bans commissions or mandates fee disclosure, as in the Netherlands
stressors.detection: European Commission consultations on the Mortgage Credit Directive and on inducements under the IDD; FSMA communications on remuneration of credit and insurance intermediaries; the Dutch provisieverbod cited in Belgian consumer press and by Test-Aankoop and Wikifin as the model for fee transparency; banks preparing direct-channel pricing that undercuts the broker channel; a requirement to disclose the referral fee in euros in the advice record; households asking in appointments what the expert earns; fee-based independent advisors positioning against 'free' brokers; and a draft law with a transition date per product line.
stressors.attractor: A directive review requires an intermediary to disclose in euros what the partner pays per contract, caps that remuneration, or, as in the Netherlands since 2013, forbids it for mortgages and complex insurance so that the consumer pays the advisor directly. 'Free for the buyer' ends on a date; 70 offices and 150 experts whose income is a commission share must become paid advisors; the comparison modules must show the fee; and a household that paid nothing must be asked to pay for a service they valued at zero. In the naive design the revenue model is one line, price is not a concept on the consumer side, the advice record does not carry the fee, the office payout has no consumer-paid component, and the monitoring service has no price.
stressors.businessReaction: Model remuneration per contract as a record with a source (partner fee, consumer fee or both), a disclosed amount and a rule version; add consumer-paid advice products, a fixed fee per mortgage file and a subscription for monitoring, that can be switched on per product line and date; show remuneration in the advice record and the comparison output as the rule requires; make the household relationship the asset that justifies a fee through savings realised and contracts watched; rework office payout so that consumer fees and partner fees flow through one rule; and run the transition as a dated programme with communication to households, partners and franchisees.
stressors.residue: Separate remuneration source, disclosed amount and rule version per contract, consumer fee product and price schedule, advice record with remuneration disclosure, payout rule spanning partner and consumer fees, and transition date per product line. Revenue becomes a rule over who pays for advice, not a fact about the trade.

impacts.effect: First-time buyers see what the advice costs and who pays it, and choose the expert for the file and the negotiated package.
Mortgage experts are paid advisors whose value is recorded per file, whichever side pays.
The best total package is presented with the remuneration disclosed as the rule requires.

stressors.name: An energy price shock or a regulated tariff wipes out the switching gain the energy comparison sells
stressors.detection: Wholesale gas and electricity prices spiking as they did in 2022; suppliers withdrawing fixed contracts and closing to new customers; a supplier failing and its customers moved to a supplier of last resort; the federal social tariff extended to more households; public debate on price caps or a regulated tariff; the spread between the cheapest and the average contract collapsing so that the 'save up to 600 euro' promise no longer holds; switch orders rejected by suppliers; callback volumes rising with questions rather than switches; the capacity tariff, digital meter and prosumer rules changing the comparison inputs; and VREG and CREG announcements.
stressors.attractor: Within weeks the cheapest contract costs more than the one the household already has, suppliers stop offering fixed contracts, one supplier goes under and its customers land with a supplier of last resort, and the government extends the social tariff and debates a cap. The comparison module still ranks contracts, the homepage still promises savings, advisors in Hasselt and Oujda spend their day explaining why not to switch, switch commissions from suppliers fall to nothing, and the savings alerts fire on stale tariffs. In the naive design the comparison is a ranking of tariffs, the promise is a fixed number, a switch is always the recommendation, energy commission is a per-switch fee that carries the brand, and the monitoring alert cannot say 'stay'.
stressors.businessReaction: Make 'do not switch' a first-class outcome with a reason and a re-check date; version tariff and product data with a validity window and the market condition they were captured under; express the savings promise as a computed range per household rather than a headline; add the capacity tariff, digital meter, social tariff and prosumer rules as versioned comparison rules; give customer care scripts that hold in a shock; treat energy commission as one of several revenue lines per household so a dead energy market does not kill the relationship; and use the contact volume to move households to the insurance and telecom savings that still exist.
stressors.residue: Separate tariff version and validity window, market condition snapshot, comparison rule version (capacity tariff, social tariff, prosumer), outcome type including stay, savings range and re-check date per household, and revenue line per contract type. A comparison is advice under a dated market condition, not a ranking.

impacts.effect: Fixed-cost savers are told to stay when staying is cheaper and are re-checked when the market turns.

stressors.name: A Google core update and the public V-check drain organic traffic from the three comparison brands
stressors.detection: Search impressions and clicks per brand falling after a core update or after AI overviews answer 'cheapest energy supplier' on the results page without a click; VREG V-check use in the tens of thousands in its first two months once the invoice code became mandatory on 1 July 2025; Wikifin's IMMOsimulator ranking above the borrowing simulator; cost per lead in paid search rising; simulator sessions and callback requests diverging between peasy.be, verzekeringen.be and aanbieders.be; reviews and directory listings drifting after the Peasy rebrand; and three domains competing with each other for the same queries.
stressors.attractor: A core update reclassifies comparison content and Google's AI overview answers the query on the results page; in the same season the V-check becomes the tool the Flemish government and the press tell households to use for energy. Aanbieders.be loses half its organic sessions, the rebrand splits authority between peasy.be and the legacy domains, paid search cannot fill the gap at the same cost per appointment, and the offices, which depend on the brand for appointments, feel it two months later. In the naive design the funnel is one number, the three brands are three websites with three content backlogs, traffic is an SEO topic rather than a demand model, and a household that once used the site has no reason to come back.
stressors.businessReaction: Model demand per brand, channel, query intent and case type with cost per appointment so spend follows what converts; run the three brands as one content and routing system with canonical pages and a rebrand migration plan; build owned channels: the customer account and contract vault, monitoring alerts, callback and chat, referrals from the 70 offices and reviews; position the expert and the switch execution as what a public tool does not do (the V-check compares, Peasy switches and keeps watching); invest in tools a public comparator lacks such as the budget barometer and upload-your-proposal; and measure the household relationship, not the session.
stressors.residue: Separate demand source and channel with cost per appointment, brand and domain routing with canonical content, owned-channel reach per household, public-tool positioning, and content lifecycle across brands. Demand is a portfolio of channels the company owns and rents, not a Google ranking.

stressors.name: Consumer AI agents compare mortgage, insurance and energy offers directly and bypass the comparator
stressors.detection: Consumer AI assistants answering 'which bank gives the best rate for 300,000 euro over 25 years' from bank websites and press rate tables; banks and insurers publishing machine-readable tariffs and agent-ready quote APIs; upload-your-proposal requests arriving already summarised by an assistant; buyers coming to appointments with an AI-drafted comparison of the 25 banks; agent traffic on the simulators; insurers piloting instant binding through assistants; and regulators discussing AI-generated financial advice under the AI Act, the IDD and the Mortgage Credit Directive.
stressors.attractor: A household asks an assistant to find the cheapest car insurance and the best mortgage for its situation; the assistant reads the tariffs the insurers now publish, requests quotes through their APIs, drafts a comparison and offers to book the switch. The comparison layer that made the three brands worth visiting is now a capability of the assistant, partners can reach the household without a broker, and the value left is what the assistant cannot do: the FSMA-regulated advice record, the bank-ready credit file, the negotiated conditions and the switch execution with cancellation of the old contract. In the naive design the comparison module is a web page for humans, partner tariffs are for internal use, the expert's know-how lives in the office, and there is no API or advice product an agent can call.
stressors.businessReaction: Expose the comparison, feasibility, quote and switch capabilities as APIs and agent-ready tools with the FSMA advice record, the expert review and the execution attached, so the assistant delegates to Peasy rather than replacing it; make partner-negotiated conditions and the daily bank feed the data an assistant cannot get elsewhere; let experts use the same assistants to prepare files and comparisons and sign them; version the advice rules and the suitability assessment so an AI-prepared comparison is reviewed and recorded like any other; and treat the assistant as a channel with its own attribution and commission terms.
stressors.residue: Separate comparison capability as a callable service with terms, agent channel and attribution, negotiated condition versus public tariff, AI-prepared draft with provenance and expert sign-off, and advice record independent of the surface it was made on. The comparison is a service with a record, not a page.

stressors.name: Scarcity of FSMA-qualified mortgage experts and franchisee churn leave offices without advisors
stressors.detection: The hypotheek.expert listed as a scarce-skill role; vacancies open for months in offices; franchisees ending or not renewing their contract; experts leaving for a bank or for a competitor with a hundred offices; the academy graduating about 30 advisors per year against the need of a network of 70 offices and the 81 of the combined group; FSMA knowledge and professional-experience requirements for credit and insurance intermediation; appointments waiting longer than a week; an office without an expert sending leads to the next town; and reviews mentioning a changed advisor.
stressors.attractor: Two experienced franchisees retire in the same quarter and three experts leave for a bank; five offices covering a region share one expert, appointments booked online cannot be served within a week, the feasibility certificate that wins houses is issued late, and the leads the brand generates go to a competitor's office nearby. Training a new expert to FSMA registration takes months, so the gap cannot be closed by hiring. In the naive design an office is a location with a person, the lead is routed by postcode, the expert's skills and registrations are an HR fact, the academy is a course calendar, and the customer's file lives in one expert's head.
stressors.businessReaction: Model expert capacity, skills and FSMA registration status per office with a regional pool so leads route to the nearest available expert, including by video; run the academy as a planned pipeline with intake cohorts, certification steps and time-to-productive per advisor sized to network churn; keep the file, the advice record and the customer's context on the platform so another expert can continue a file; offer franchise succession and office takeover paths so a retiring franchisee does not close an office; make video appointments from a central pool the fallback for any office; and measure expert retention and time-to-fill as network health.
stressors.residue: Separate expert capacity, skill and registration status, regional expert pool and video fallback, academy cohort, certification step and time-to-productive, office succession record, file continuity across experts, and expert retention and time-to-fill metrics. An office is a coverage the network guarantees, not a person who happens to be there.

stressors.name: A data breach exposes credit files with income, savings, national register numbers and health questions
stressors.detection: Phishing against expert and customer-care logins across about 70 offices and two care centres; bulk downloads of credit-file documents outside office hours; a franchisee's laptop or mailbox compromised; documents forwarded to banks by e-mail; a supplier incident at the e-signature, telephony or hosting provider; the 72-hour notification duty to the Belgian Data Protection Authority; households asking who saw their payslips; FSMA and the FPS Economy asking for the intermediary's records; and health questionnaires for outstanding-balance insurance stored next to the mortgage file.
stressors.attractor: A phished expert account in one office is used to export hundreds of credit files: payslips, tax returns, savings statements, national register numbers, EPC certificates and the health questionnaires for outstanding-balance insurance. Peasy must tell each household what was taken, notify the authority within 72 hours, answer the banks whose customers these are, and defend the trust the phygital brand is built on, across three brands and a franchise network where the office is a separate company. In the naive design access follows the office, documents are files in a folder, exports are not logged per document, health data sits with financial data, retention is a policy nobody executes, and a franchisee is outside the security perimeter.
stressors.businessReaction: Contain and revoke, determine affected records per household from access and export logs, and notify households, banks, insurers and the authority with evidence; scope expert and advisor access per file, task and period with step-up authentication for exports and identity documents; classify data by class with national register number, health questions and identity documents at the highest level and keep insurance health data separate from the mortgage file; log every view and export; execute retention per class against FSMA record-keeping duties; extend the security perimeter to franchise offices by contract and by tooling; and rehearse the response with the network and the partners.
stressors.residue: Separate data class, access scope by file, task and period, step-up authentication event, view and export event, retention rule per data class, incident, affected-record set and notification, and franchise security obligation. Access is a relationship between a person, a file and a task, and every export is a record.

stressors.name: The Meilleurtaux acquisition merges two networks, two brands and two workbenches into one national platform
stressors.detection: The agreement of 23 December 2025 for Meilleurtaux to acquire 100 percent of Peasy; 81 combined offices with Meilleurtaux mainly in Wallonia and Peasy in Flanders and Brussels; David Geerts leading Belgium and Luxembourg; overlapping bank and insurer relationships with different commission agreements; two credit-file processes and two workbenches; consumer credit and credit grouping arriving as new product lines; a group brand decision pending; French-language content and Walloon offices joining a Dutch-first platform; and integration workstreams competing with the roadmap.
stressors.attractor: The group decides that one workbench, one lead engine and one brand will serve 81 offices in both languages within eighteen months, that consumer credit and credit grouping go live in Flanders, and that bank agreements are renegotiated at group level. Files in flight must not be lost, offices in Wallonia follow a different process, commission statements arrive under two agreements for the same bank, and the product teams are asked to migrate while keeping three brands running. In the naive design there is one company, one workbench, Dutch first with French translated, one agreement per bank, and a brick's data model is the company's.
stressors.businessReaction: Model brand, legal entity, office and network membership separately so an office can belong to either company and any brand during the transition; keep a shared identity and customer registry across both platforms; map concepts (file, case, advice record, commission) between the two workbenches and migrate files with lineage and a rollback; run partner agreements per legal entity with a group view; add consumer credit and credit grouping as case types with their own advice rules; make French a first-class locale rather than a translation; and run integration as a dated programme with parity checks per capability before any sunset.
stressors.residue: Separate brand, legal entity and network membership, shared customer and identity registry, concept mapping and migration lineage, agreement per legal entity with group view, case type and product line, locale as first-class, and capability parity and sunset plan. The platform is a group of entities and brands sharing records, not one company's system.

stressors.name: A partner tariff feed or bank rate feed goes wrong and the comparison sells prices that do not exist
stressors.detection: A bank's daily rate sheet arriving late, empty or in a new format; an insurer's quote API timing out or returning test tariffs; an energy supplier publishing a tariff card with an error; comparison results changing overnight without a partner announcement; experts noticing that the on-screen rate differs from the bank's own offer; switch orders rejected by a supplier; quotes bound at a premium the insurer disputes; commission disputes on contracts sold under the wrong tariff; and monitoring alerts fired from a wrong feed.
stressors.attractor: On a Monday the rate feed of two banks fails silently and the comparison engine keeps ranking Friday's rates while the banks raised them; an insurer's quote API returns test tariffs; and the energy module ingests a tariff card with a decimal error, so that for two days households are told to switch to a contract that is ten percent more expensive. Experts issue proposals the bank will not honour, customer care binds policies at the wrong premium, the monitoring engine sends savings alerts that are wrong, and the partner asks who pays. Under the tariff version and validity window from the energy shock and the agreement version and expected commission per file from the commission cut, the platform can tell which comparisons, proposals, quotes and switches were made under which feed version and re-quote or honour them by policy.
stressors.businessReaction: Validate every feed and quote against its previous version and plausibility rules before it reaches a comparison, quarantine anomalies, mark results as stale when a feed is late, stamp every proposal, quote, switch and alert with the feed version it used, notify partners and affected households from that stamp, re-quote or honour by policy, and reconcile disputed commissions against the feed version. No new residues are needed; the loop confirms that tariff versioning and expected-commission records hold.
stressors.residue: Reuses tariff version and validity window, market condition snapshot and stay outcome from the energy shock, and partner agreement version, expected commission per file and statement reconciliation from the commission cut, adding only feed validation and quarantine as operations on those records.
